## Available rendered final

Result

I developed a specific removal mechanism, a complete process construction, and an executable campaign and factory model. I cannot honestly call the result the economical, qualified reuse operation you requested. The constructed reference case misses the capital, service-cost and campaign-energy targets substantially. Its potentially useful invention is a support-transfer mechanism that releases the original joint one lamination at a time while continuously supporting the brittle magnets.

The work also exposes two independent obstacles: the selected rotor’s proprietary material and bonding details remain insufficiently characterized, and its available population cannot sustain the requested single-family industrial throughput for 20 years.

1. The concrete available relay

The described rotor-removal construction engages one0.28mm lamination with twelve jaws while24individual pins support magnet columns. A separate comb takes the support before pins retract to permit collector exchange. Pins return through the empty collector before the comb withdraws. Later broad grips transfer around a final collar so a three-sided cut, grip change and final cut have an actual access path. These are specified but unqualified mechanical operations. A low total force does not bound the load on a particular jammed support, and an immovable supporting tool can block the final removal path.

The reference slice area is2(w+t)h=12.18mm2 forw18.7,t3.05,h.28mm. Introduced10MPa effective shear gives121.8N, while22MPa gives267.96N, beyond the introduced200N individual-pin limit. No actual aged resin/crack-path/coating stress is measured. Multiple-plate bonding and accumulated6.684m edge travel over a bar remain material and wear operations. The20-year finance horizon does not logically require one historical rotor family forever, but paid changes of feed family, fixtures and qualification are necessary if that scenario uses a finite source population.

Source statements and magnetic/coupler/EDM/coating results retain the available producer's actual exposure, not a ROOT governing read of those originals.
